opening.text: Picture a car with a dead engine on a country road. It cannot move on its own. Then a truck stops and ties a strong rope between the two. The engine is still dead. But the car begins to roll. The power is not coming from the car. It is coming through the rope.
Many of us feel like that car. We look at our weakness and think we have little to give. Today we will see that God can use that very place to reach us.

mainMessage.text: Weakness is not proof that God has left. It is where His grace can do its work. We were never asked to fix ourselves alone. We are asked to stay tied to Him and let Him pull.

blocks.text: **Weakness has a purpose.** The dead engine shows the driver where help is needed. In the same way, God lets us see our weakness so we will turn to Him. He does not show it to shame us. He shows it to teach us.

And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Our greatest weaknesses can become our greatest strengths.
The weakness is the reason we reach for the rope.
**The rope does not break.** Paul begged to have his trial taken away. God gave him something better. He gave him grace that was enough. The rope holds because of His strength, not ours.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
His grace is indeed sufficient.
We do not have to be strong enough. His grace is.

**He does not scold the stalled car.** The driver does not stop to lecture. He stops to help. Still, he does not leave the car on the road either. God loves us just as we are. And He loves us too much to let us stay stuck.
Behold ye shall answer this question yourselves; nevertheless, I will be merciful unto you; he that is weak among you hereafter shall be made strong.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
God loves us as we are, but He also loves us too much to leave us this way.
His love stays with us, and it moves us forward.

**The pull starts now.** The truck does not wait until the engine is repaired. It pulls the car while the car is still broken. Help from God works the same way. We do not need to get ready first. We can ask today.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Most important, remember that God and Christ are willing to help us right here and now.
Right here means in the place where we are stuck.

**We cannot pull ourselves.** No one can sit in a car and lift it by tugging on the steering wheel. We try that with our own lives sometimes. We think we must make ourselves perfect first. It is not possible, and we were never asked to do it.

Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness; and if ye shall deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and love God with all your might, mind and strength, then is his grace sufficient for you, that by his grace ye may be perfect in Christ; and if by the grace of God ye are perfect in Christ, ye can in nowise deny the power of God.
Elder Paul V. Johnson, of the Presidency of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Be Perfected in Him” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We may have a tendency to think we have to perfect ourselves, but that is not possible.
We do our part. Christ does the part we cannot.

**Slow is still moving.** A tow can be slow. The road can have hills. Some days the rope pulls us forward and some days it feels like we slip back. That is part of the trip, and it does not mean the trip has failed.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Sometimes it may feel like two steps forward and one step back, but we continue to humbly move forward in faith.
We keep holding the rope.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt weak and found help from God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Moses Says He Cannot Speak Well

blocks.text: Moses did not think he was the right person. He said he was slow of speech. God did not agree that this made him the wrong choice.

And Moses said unto the Lord, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. And the Lord said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the Lord? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
Moses named his weakness. God answered with a promise to be with him. The rope was already tied.

application.text: First, name one weakness you are tired of fighting alone. Say it plainly in prayer and ask God to help you with it today.
Second, do one small thing this week that is within your reach. Then trust Christ with the part that is not.
Third, if you slip back, do not quit. Ask again. If the weight feels too heavy, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God sees our weakness and does not turn away. I know that the grace of Jesus Christ is enough. I have felt His help in places where I could not move on my own. I know that weak things can become strong when we turn to Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A child learns to ride a bike with training wheels. Nobody sees that as a failure. The extra wheels keep the bike steady while balance grows. After a while the child rides with confidence and a parent running close behind.
We are a little different from that child. We do not outgrow our need for help. But we do grow closer to the One who steadies us. Let us look at how that works.

mainMessage.text: Having a weakness is not shameful. It is part of being mortal. Christ steadies us, and as we lean on Him, we become stronger than we could be alone.

blocks.text: **Weak spots keep us humble.** Training wheels remind a rider that balance is not yet perfect. Our weak spots do the same. They remind us who we depend on. That reminder is a gift if we use it well.

And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Our greatest weaknesses can become our greatest strengths.
What felt like a flaw can become a place of strength.

**There is enough for every day.** A rider does not need to know how to ride a hundred miles. The next block is enough. Paul learned that God’s grace was enough for each day, even while his trial stayed.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
His grace is indeed sufficient.
We can trust that today’s grace will be there today.

**A loving parent runs alongside.** A parent holding the bike does not shame the child for wobbling. The parent also does not want the child to wobble forever. God loves us in the same way. He accepts us where we are, and He wants more for us.
Behold ye shall answer this question yourselves; nevertheless, I will be merciful unto you; he that is weak among you hereafter shall be made strong.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
God loves us as we are, but He also loves us too much to leave us this way.
He does both at the same time.

**Help is on the bike today.** Training wheels are not saved for the day a child is ready. They are there from the first wobble. Heavenly help is the same. It is available before we feel strong enough to deserve it.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Most important, remember that God and Christ are willing to help us right here and now.
We do not have to wait to ask.

**Perfecting is His work.** A child cannot build a bike by sitting on it and wishing. Some things must be given. In the same way, we cannot make ourselves perfect. We come to Christ, and He does what we cannot.

Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness; and if ye shall deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and love God with all your might, mind and strength, then is his grace sufficient for you, that by his grace ye may be perfect in Christ; and if by the grace of God ye are perfect in Christ, ye can in nowise deny the power of God.
Elder Paul V. Johnson, of the Presidency of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Be Perfected in Him” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We may have a tendency to think we have to perfect ourselves, but that is not possible.
That is not bad news. It is a relief.
**Falls are part of learning.** Every rider falls. The question is whether the rider gets back on. Our growth in Christ has the same pattern. We go forward, we slip, and we try again with Him.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Sometimes it may feel like two steps forward and one step back, but we continue to humbly move forward in faith.
We get back on and keep going.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt too small for something and found help from God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Gideon, the Least in His Father’s House

blocks.text: Gideon was asked to save his people. He pointed to his small, poor family and to himself as the least in it. God did not argue with the facts. He gave a promise.

And he said unto him, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house. And the Lord said unto him, Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man.
The promise was not that Gideon would become big. It was that God would be with him.

application.text: First, think of one area where you feel unsteady. Write it down and ask God what the next small step could be.
Second, let someone steady you. Tell a trusted friend or family member what you are working on.
Third, when you fall, get back up the same day. Pray, try again, and trust Christ to run alongside you. If you need more help, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that Jesus Christ does not leave us alone when we wobble. I know His grace is enough for today. I have seen weak places in my life become places where I felt His strength. I know He will keep helping us as we keep trying. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: You know the feeling of a phone at two percent. It dims. It slows down. It cannot do much on its own. Then you plug it in, and within minutes it comes back to life. The phone did not become stronger by trying harder. It received power from a source outside itself.
Our spirits can run low in the same way. When we feel drained and weak, there is a Source we can plug into. Let us see what the scriptures and our leaders teach about that.

mainMessage.text: We are not meant to run on our own power. Christ gives strength to those who come to Him, and He does it again each day. Our weakness is not the end of the story. It is where we find out how much He gives.

blocks.text: **Low power shows us where to plug in.** A low battery is a signal, not a disgrace. Our weakness is a signal too. It tells us it is time to turn to God. When we do, He can make us strong in ways we did not expect.

And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Our greatest weaknesses can become our greatest strengths.
The signal is there to help us, not to harm us.

**The supply does not run out.** A charger works as long as it is connected to power. God’s grace is like that. Paul asked for his thorn to be removed. Instead, he was told that grace was enough. He found that out by living it.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
His grace is indeed sufficient.
There is always enough.

**He loves the phone and wants it to work.** Nobody throws away a phone for having a low battery. Nobody wants it to stay at two percent either. God loves us as we are. Because He loves us, He also wants to help us grow.
Behold ye shall answer this question yourselves; nevertheless, I will be merciful unto you; he that is weak among you hereafter shall be made strong.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
God loves us as we are, but He also loves us too much to leave us this way.
He loves us enough to help us change.

**Plug in right away.** You do not wait for the battery to improve before you charge it. You plug it in at once. God’s help is just as ready. We can turn to Him in the middle of a hard morning or a long night.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Most important, remember that God and Christ are willing to help us right here and now.
No waiting room. No wait time.

**A phone cannot charge itself.** It does not matter how hard a phone tries. It needs a source outside itself. We cannot reach perfection by willpower alone either. Only Christ can finish that work in us.

Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness; and if ye shall deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and love God with all your might, mind and strength, then is his grace sufficient for you, that by his grace ye may be perfect in Christ; and if by the grace of God ye are perfect in Christ, ye can in nowise deny the power of God.
Elder Paul V. Johnson, of the Presidency of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Be Perfected in Him” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We may have a tendency to think we have to perfect ourselves, but that is not possible.
Our part is to stay connected.

**Charge a little each day.** A phone does not stay full forever. We plug it in again and again. Spiritual strength works that way too. We go back to God in prayer and scripture, day after day. Some days feel like progress. Some days feel like a step back. We keep coming back.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Sometimes it may feel like two steps forward and one step back, but we continue to humbly move forward in faith.
Daily connection brings steady strength.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they ran low and found strength from God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: David and the Five Smooth Stones

blocks.text: David was a shepherd boy facing a giant. He did not put on a soldier’s armor. He took what he knew how to use. He trusted that God was with him.

And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine. And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
David looked small next to Goliath. But he was not alone, and that made all the difference.

application.text: First, notice when you feel drained. Pause and say a short prayer right then, even one sentence.
Second, build a small daily habit that keeps you connected to God. A few verses or a few quiet minutes will do.
Third, when you feel too low to try, ask for help anyway. If the weight feels heavy for a long time, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God gives strength to the weary. I know His grace is enough, even on my lowest days. I have learned that I do not have to carry everything on my own power. I know that Jesus Christ is the Source of lasting strength. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A hiker with a sore knee reaches a steep, rocky trail. She has two choices. She can turn back, or she can take a walking stick. With the stick taking some of her weight, she keeps climbing. The knee is still sore. But she reaches the top.
When we are hurting or weak, we often think we must stop. The gospel offers another way. We can take hold of the One who bears our weight.

mainMessage.text: Leaning on Christ is not weakness. It is wisdom. The One who made us knows where we are fragile, and He walks with us up the hard parts.

blocks.text: **Admitting the sore knee.** A hiker who pretends nothing hurts will soon fall. A hiker who admits the pain can find a way forward. When we are honest about our weakness, we make room for God to help.

And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Our greatest weaknesses can become our greatest strengths.
Honesty is where the climb begins.

**The stick is always long enough.** A good walking stick does not break halfway up the hill. Christ’s grace does not either. Paul leaned on it through a trial that never left, and he found it was enough.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
His grace is indeed sufficient.
We can put our weight on it.

**A guide who loves the hiker.** A good guide does not mock a slow hiker. A good guide also does not want her to stay at the bottom of the mountain. God loves us as we are. And He has a higher place in mind for us.
Behold ye shall answer this question yourselves; nevertheless, I will be merciful unto you; he that is weak among you hereafter shall be made strong.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
God loves us as we are, but He also loves us too much to leave us this way.
He wants us at the top with Him.

**Take the stick on the first step.** The hiker does not wait until her knee heals. She uses the stick from the first rock. Heavenly help is available to us in the same way. We do not need to be better before we ask.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Most important, remember that God and Christ are willing to help us right here and now.
The path starts under our feet.

**We do not carry the mountain.** The hiker walks, but she does not move the mountain. Some things are beyond us. Making us whole and complete is the Savior’s work. We walk beside Him, and He does what we cannot.

Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness; and if ye shall deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and love God with all your might, mind and strength, then is his grace sufficient for you, that by his grace ye may be perfect in Christ; and if by the grace of God ye are perfect in Christ, ye can in nowise deny the power of God.
Elder Paul V. Johnson, of the Presidency of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Be Perfected in Him” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We may have a tendency to think we have to perfect ourselves, but that is not possible.
We climb. He carries what we cannot.
**Some steps are slow.** On a steep trail, some steps go sideways or back. A good hiker does not call that failure. She plants the stick and tries again. Progress in faith looks much the same.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Sometimes it may feel like two steps forward and one step back, but we continue to humbly move forward in faith.
We keep climbing.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a weakness stayed with them but God still blessed them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jacob Wrestles and Walks Away Blessed

blocks.text: Jacob wrestled through the night and would not let go until he received a blessing. The struggle left him with a limp. But he left with God’s blessing too.

And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.
Jacob walked away with a limp and a blessing. The two were not at odds. The limp reminded him where the blessing came from.

application.text: First, name the “sore knee” you have been hiding. Tell God about it honestly.
Second, ask what your walking stick could be this week. It might be a prayer, a scripture, or a friend you trust.
Third, take one step on the hard trail today, even a small one. If you feel stuck, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that Jesus Christ walks with us up the hard parts of the trail. I know His grace holds our weight. I have leaned on Him when I could not go on alone. I know that He is able to make weak things strong. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A sail is only a sheet of thin cloth. By itself it cannot move a boat an inch. But when a sailor sets it right and the wind fills it, that thin cloth can carry a heavy boat across a wide lake.
The strength is not in the cloth. It is in the wind. The sailor’s work is to raise the sail and turn it the right way. Our lives can work like that with God.

mainMessage.text: We may feel as thin and weak as cloth. That is all right. God’s power fills what is open to Him. When we set ourselves toward Him, He can carry us farther than we could go alone.

blocks.text: **A sail has no power of its own.** Cloth does not need to pretend to be an engine. In the same way, we do not need to pretend we are strong. God lets us see where we are weak so we will open ourselves to Him.

And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Our greatest weaknesses can become our greatest strengths.
Thin cloth, filled with wind, can cross a lake.

**The wind is enough.** A sailor does not need a bigger sail to reach the far shore. The wind does the work. Paul learned that Christ’s grace was enough for him. He did not need more strength of his own.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
His grace is indeed sufficient.
We do not need to add to it.

**The captain loves the boat and wants it to sail.** A captain does not scorn a plain boat. A captain also does not want it to sit at the dock. God loves us as we are. Because He loves us, He wants to take us somewhere better.
Behold ye shall answer this question yourselves; nevertheless, I will be merciful unto you; he that is weak among you hereafter shall be made strong.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
God loves us as we are, but He also loves us too much to leave us this way.
He loves us enough to move us.

**Raise the sail today.** A sailor does not wait for a perfect boat. The sail goes up now, and the wind meets it. God is ready to help us as soon as we turn toward Him. We do not have to wait for a better day.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

Brother Bradley R. Wilcox, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency, said this in his talk “Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness” from the October 2021 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Most important, remember that God and Christ are willing to help us right here and now.
The wind is already blowing.

**No sailor makes the wind.** The best sailor in the world cannot create a breeze. The sailor can only be ready for it. We cannot make ourselves perfect in the same way. We come to Christ, and His grace carries us where we cannot go ourselves.

Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness; and if ye shall deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and love God with all your might, mind and strength, then is his grace sufficient for you, that by his grace ye may be perfect in Christ; and if by the grace of God ye are perfect in Christ, ye can in nowise deny the power of God.
Elder Paul V. Johnson, of the Presidency of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Be Perfected in Him” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We may have a tendency to think we have to perfect ourselves, but that is not possible.
Our part is to be ready. His part is the power.

**Sailing is not a straight line.** When the wind blows against a boat, a good sailor zigzags. The boat goes one way, then another, and still moves ahead. Our growth often looks like that. Some days feel like a step back. The trip is still going forward.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Kevin S. Hamilton of the Seventy said this in his talk “Then Will I Make Weak Things Become Strong” from the April 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Sometimes it may feel like two steps forward and one step back, but we continue to humbly move forward in faith.
We keep the sail up.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt weak and still moved forward with God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi Admits His Weakness and Trusts God

blocks.text: Nephi saw many marvelous things. Still, he felt his own weakness deeply. He did not hide it. He said it out loud, and then he said what he knew about God.

Nevertheless, notwithstanding the great goodness of the Lord, in showing me his great and marvelous works, my heart exclaimeth: O wretched man that I am! Yea, my heart sorroweth because of my flesh; my soul grieveth because of mine iniquities. I am encompassed about, because of the temptations and the sins which do so easily beset me. And when I desire to rejoice, my heart groaneth because of my sins; nevertheless, I know in whom I have trusted.
Nephi felt weak, and he said so. But he did not stop there. He ended with the words, “I know in whom I have trusted.”

application.text: First, say your weakness out loud to God, the way Nephi did. Then say what you know about Him.
Second, set your “sail” each morning. Ask Him to help you with one thing you cannot do alone today.
Third, when the wind seems to be against you, keep going. Small turns still move you forward. If you need more help, speak with your bishop or branch president.
